response.rationale: The heli surveys from tick 0 to 2, so the world is known at tick 2. The crew opens airstrip and the dozer opens farm in both worlds, and the heli then runs switchyard (worth 211 in both worlds) at tick 6. In beta, the dozer opens orchard then quarry, which allows substation (208) and clinic (169); kiln is given up there. In alpha, the dozer opens bridge for kiln and silo, and the team adds hospital, mill and other alpha-only jobs. Each world uses exactly 11 units of water on its most valuable water jobs. Expected value is 0.4 × 860 + 0.6 × 923 ≈ 897.8.

Engine-1 runs survey 539 from tick 0, so the true wind corridor is known at tick 3. Until then, every team does work that pays off in both worlds: chapel, dairy, museum and yard access, plus the relay wetline. From tick 3, each corridor gets its own schedule. Alpha does camp, intake, quarry, marina, cabin, silo, orchard and pumphouse. Beta does hospital, kiln, quarry, orchard, substation, mill and switchyard (via the winery access). The heli spends exactly the 11 units of water in each world on that world's best wetlines.

Heli surveys at tick 0 so the world is known at tick 2, while pre-reveal teams build the shared access chain (yard, chapel, dairy then museum) and the engine lays relay. Quarry (engine 6-10) and orchard (crew-1 3-8) run in both worlds. In alpha the plan takes camp, intake, marina, cabin, silo, pumphouse and the alpha wetlines; in beta it takes kiln, hospital, substation, mill and winery then switchyard, plus the beta wetlines. Water is fully used (11) in each world; farm is the one alpha job knowingly dropped because yard takes crew-1's first slot.

Access chain is scheduled first so quarry (415) completes by tick 10, which makes the beta-only substation (769) and clinic (850) startable at the reveal-driven tick 10. Switchyard (827) and kiln (783) run on heli-1 after airstrip, farm and bridge finish. Water is used exactly up to 11 by both-world wetlines. Alpha-only and beta-only entries start at or after the bulletin tick 9. Plant (830), chapel (525) and foundry (543) are omitted because no team can fit them without breaking the access chain. Expected value is about 965 in my hand estimate, and several dependencies finish exactly at a start tick, so I am relying on completion at tick t counting as completed by tick t.

Hand-built schedule that runs the high-value chains (chapel→camp/quarry/intake/cabin, dairy→museum→quarry/intake, yard→orchard/hospital/granary) in both worlds, and uses the engine-1 window 3–6 and 6–10 for camp then quarry. Heli-1 runs the water jobs in sequence and uses exactly 11 water in alpha and 10 in beta. Only the forecast-dependent choices are branch-specific: shelter (alpha) and vineyard (beta) share the heli slot at tick 9, pumphouse is alpha-only, and mill is beta-only; all world-specific starts are at or after the bulletin tick 8. No survey is bought because its 3-unit cost outweighs the small gain from earlier reveal. Expected net value is roughly 757 units; feasibility was checked tick by tick for team overlaps, prerequisites, deadlines and water.

No survey: every beta-leaning job is still net positive in alpha, and the alpha-only jobs (bakery, school, pumphouse) can wait for the tick-9 bulletin. Dozer does farm, airstrip, quarry and crew does orchard, bridge, which unlocks switchyard, kiln, hospital, substation and clinic in time; only chapel, plant and foundry are given up. After the bulletin, dozer does clinic in beta or bakery in alpha, with school and pumphouse (alpha) or station (beta) late. The 11 water goes to relay, marina, switchyard, kiln, yard, granary and hatchery.

Heli-1 surveys at tick 0, so the world is known at tick 2. Work that pays in both worlds is fixed: marina, yard then switchyard, shelter, bakery, school and plant. In alpha, dozer-2 builds airstrip then station so chapel and camp can finish by tick 14, and water goes to marina, stable, dairy, mill and chapel. In beta, water goes to marina, mill and orchard, and the other teams cover winery, granary, foundry, library, sawmill and depot, with small fill-in jobs where teams are free.

The survey reveals the corridor at tick 2, enabling the beta access chain while reserving alpha capacity for the bakery, school, and pumphouse. Every entry is feasible, and each world uses exactly 11 water. Expected net protected value is 964.6: 862 in alpha and 1033 in beta.

The survey reveals the corridor at tick 3, enabling timely world-specific assignments while preserving the major prerequisite chains. Every entry executes feasibly, using exactly 11 water in each world. Net protected value is 949 in alpha and 596 in beta, for an expected value of 807.8.

No survey: its 5-point cost and 2-tick heli slot buy little, since the bulletin reveals the forecast at tick 10 anyway. Water (11) is spent on marina, mill, chapel, stable (both) and dairy (alpha-only at 10). Dozer-1 chains yard, switchyard, sawmill, bakery, vineyard, tower, school, plant; dozer-2 chains airstrip, station, depot, clinic. Engine-1 runs winery, library, granary; crew-1 runs shelter, lodge, camp. Pre-reveal jobs are "both" because their expected net is highest that way. Dropped: reservoir and museum (infeasible), relay, cabin, foundry, orchard and farm (no slot or water).

Heli-1 surveys at tick 0 so the corridor is known at tick 2, while crew starts shelter and dozer-1 opens yard for switchyard in both worlds. Beta: engine runs foundry, winery, granary, crew adds library, dozer-2 takes depot, and water goes to marina, mill and orchard. Lodge is dropped in beta because engine and crew cannot fit all six protect jobs; reservoir, museum and substation are infeasible or not worth the water.

After the tick-10 bulletin, alpha adds clinic, yard, orchard, sawmill, village, dairy and museum; beta adds quarry, sawmill, shelter, foundry and dairy. Expected net value is about 1069.

Bakery is out because it uses 3 water and its start must be at tick 1 or earlier, which is before the reveal. Station (both worlds) plus alpha-only museum and lodge use the full 5 water, which beats bakery in expectation. I skipped early surveys because the reveal at tick 10 still lets every world-specific job start in time. Substation, quarry and pumphouse are "both" to capture the beta value. Alpha-only and beta-only entries reuse the same team slots, so tower (alpha) and foundry (beta) share engine-1 at ticks 11-14.

Heli survey 498 at tick 0 reveals the corridor at tick 2, so alpha-only jobs (bakery and its farm access, silo-level extras, switchyard, vineyard, observatory, substation, lodge) and beta-only jobs (kiln, shelter, library, camp) run only in their world. No survey: every world-specific choice can wait until the tick-10 bulletin, so the only blind waste is three cheap alpha-leaning engine jobs (425, 448, 200), costing 6 in beta, which is less in expectation than a survey's cost of 4 in both worlds. Expected net is about 1092.5 (alpha 1066, beta 1119).

Water (13) is fully used by station, pumphouse, clinic, reservoir, winery, cabin and beta-only camp. Every entry starts exactly when its team and prerequisites are free, so no executor shifts occur.
Expected net protected value is 991: 1060 in alpha and 922 in beta. Branches use the tick-10 bulletin; every scheduled entry executes feasibly, consuming five water units in alpha and three in beta.
